solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Lace clothing of empress in photo call (10)

indicatorNotes.clothing of: the clothing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in: the outer letters go inside the next piece

blocks.note: to ring is to call on the phone

annotation.surface: A royal photo shoot where everyone is fussing over the empress's lace outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Lace' sound like fabric on the empress; it is the noun for the cord in a shoe. 'In photo' means inside the photo word, not in the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the footwear sense: the string that ties a shoe, not the lace fabric the empress is wearing.

entries.clue: Cast piece of armour abandoned by lake (5)

indicatorNotes.abandoned by: the lake letter is left behind, so it drops out

blocks.note: a shield is a piece of armour

annotation.surface: A knight's bit of armour, cast aside and left by a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as thrown off, which it is: to shy something is to throw it, so SHIED is the past tense.
annotation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy, so shied means cast.

entries.clue: Some journalists in a group sent up key workers (9)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the phrase are used
indicatorNotes.sent up: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters inside journaliSTS IN A GROup

annotation.surface: A pack of reporters mocking the essential staff of a pandemic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key workers' suggests essential staff; organists work keys on an organ.
annotation.definitionFit: Organists play keyboards, so they are workers at keys.

entries.clue: Ostracised soldier burying explosive around old bay (4,2,8)

indicatorNotes.burying: the soldier holds the rest buried inside him
indicatorNotes.around: the explosive wraps around the old bay

blocks.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard
a cove is a small bay

annotation.surface: A soldier shunned by his unit after hiding explosives near an old bay.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the explosive wraps the old bay, and the soldier buries the lot. To send someone to Coventry, an English city, is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them.
annotation.definitionFit: To be sent to Coventry is to be ostracised, deliberately ignored by everyone.

entries.clue: Lots of ferries originally circled by shoal quickly list (4,3)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the original, first letter of each word
indicatorNotes.circled by: the reef goes around those letters

blocks.note: a shoal is a sandbank or reef
first letters of Lots Of Ferries

annotation.surface: A fleet of ferries trapped behind a sandbank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Originally' applies to all three words before it, not just 'ferries'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from fishing: line spinning off a reel, so a speaker rattling items off without pause.

entries.clue: Males recalled wings of enormous island deity (7)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.wings of: the wings of a word are its two ends

annotation.surface: Men recalled from a vast island shrine where some great god was worshipped.
annotation.walkthrough: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution.
annotation.definitionFit: Nemesis is the Greek goddess of retribution, so a deity.

entries.clue: Drop beer on the counter (4)

indicatorNotes.on the counter: running counter to the normal direction, so backwards

annotation.surface: Spilling a pint on the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a bar top; it means backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: To slip is to drop, as prices slip or a standard drops.

entries.clue: Master essentially coerces spare guards (5)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its middle
indicatorNotes.guards: the outer word holds the letter inside it

blocks.note: lean and spare both mean thin

annotation.surface: A slave-owner forcing a thin servant to stand guard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a noun at the start; it is the verb, to get the hang of something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: getting the hang of a subject, not the noun for a boss.

entries.clue: Picked up harmony note inside of hall gradually (9)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear, heard, so a sound-alike
indicatorNotes.inside of: take the letters from the inside of the word

blocks.note: peace is harmony, and sounds like piece
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: Hearing a harmonious note slowly fill a concert hall.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical words (harmony, note, hall) all point to a concert; only 'harmony' is heard, the rest are read.
annotation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means bit by bit, gradually.

entries.clue: Snag small navel decoration perhaps on black hair (9,5)

blocks.note: bling (flashy jewellery) on a tum (tummy) is a navel decoration, like a belly-button ring
a lock is a tress of hair

annotation.surface: Catching a tiny belly-button piercing in someone's dark hair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags TUM BLING as one invented example of navel decoration rather than a dictionary phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a hidden difficulty that trips a plan up, which is the unexpected-problem sense of snag.

entries.clue: Green female wearing uniform pressed by Vincent? (7)

indicatorNotes.pressed by: the uniform letter is squeezed inside Vincent's first name

blocks.note: in = wearing, as in 'in a hat'
Gene Vincent was an American rock and roll singer
U = uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A woman whose uniform has been ironed by someone called Vincent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vincent?' wants Van Gogh; the question mark says Vincent is a surname here, so GENE. Green means naive.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, inexperienced young woman, a green female.

entries.clue: Setter and former land owner lower emission (7)

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a thane held land from a king in Anglo-Saxon and Scottish times

annotation.surface: The puzzle-setter and an old laird cutting their carbon output.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as a verb, to reduce emissions; it is an adjective, emission from the lower body, a wind joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Methane is released when a person or a cow breaks wind, an emission from the lower end.

entries.clue: Fellow American is not moving drawings from vessels? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the question mark flags a definition by example: blood donations

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

annotation.surface: An American academic sitting still, sketching pictures of ships.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawings' suggests sketches and 'vessels' ships; the vessels are blood vessels, and the drawings are blood being drawn.
annotation.definitionFit: Blood donations are drawn from the donor's veins, so drawings from vessels.

entries.clue: Vicar’s digs maybe woman senses to some extent (5)

indicatorNotes.to some extent: only part of the phrase is used

annotation.surface: A woman partly picking up on something odd at the vicarage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' because a manse is strictly a Scottish or Nonconformist minister's house, not a vicar's; digs are lodgings.
annotation.definitionFit: A manse is a clergyman's house, so a vicar's lodgings, broadly.

entries.clue: Radical writer introducing case for aesthetics (5)

indicatorNotes.introducing: the pen takes the other letters into itself
indicatorNotes.case for: the case of a word is its outside letters

blocks.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen

annotation.surface: A revolutionary author bringing an argument for beauty into the debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is not political here: a radical change is a basic, fundamental one.
annotation.definitionFit: Radical means of the root, fundamental, basic.

entries.clue: Ceramic hob in Caen needing repair (4,5)

indicatorNotes.needing repair: the letters are broken and must be put back together differently

annotation.surface: A cooker hob in a French kitchen that has broken down.
annotation.walkthrough: Caen is a city in Normandy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by kind: porcelain made with bone ash belongs to the wider class of fired pottery.

entries.clue: Bond catches one youth crossing large barrage (9)

indicatorNotes.catches: the bond holds the rest inside
indicatorNotes.crossing: the youth comes across, meeting the large letter side by side

annotation.surface: James Bond grabbing a young man running over a big dam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bond' wants the spy and 'barrage' a dam; they are a verb and a burst of gunfire.
annotation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a rapid series of shots, a barrage.

entries.clue: Artist is overwhelmed by shock valuation (9)

indicatorNotes.is overwhelmed by: the shock word swamps the other letters, holding them inside

annotation.surface: A painter stunned when told what the work is worth.
annotation.walkthrough: The artist is overwhelmed at the valuation in the surface; in the wordplay the artist and 'is' are literally inside APPAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an expert's estimate of what something is worth, as for insurance.

entries.clue: New tree beginning to leaf inside of foul city (9)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the L of leaf is used
indicatorNotes.inside of: that letter goes inside the next word

annotation.surface: A young tree coming into leaf in a grimy city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside of foul' tempts a reading of the middle letters of foul; it means L goes inside VILE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital of Tennessee, home of country music.

entries.clue: Throw back mostly what may have been in pot (7)

annotation.definition: what may have been in pot

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: STERN, the back of a boat, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Tossing back most of a catch from a fisherman's pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw back' reads as one phrase about returning a fish; split it, and 'back' is the stern.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint by example: lobster pots are the traps crustaceans are caught in, and 'may have been' allows for a cooking pot too.

entries.clue: Wandering about over grass covering centre of domicile (7)

indicatorNotes.covering: in a down answer, the grass sits on top of the next piece
indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of an even-length word is its middle pair, so IC from domicile

blocks.note: to grass and to rat are both to inform on someone
the middle two letters of domICile

annotation.surface: Someone drifting around, walking across the lawn to the middle of a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a lawn; it is the slang verb for informing, so RAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Erratic means wandering, irregular, not keeping a fixed course.

entries.clue: Pole joining another cycling in country (5)

indicatorNotes.joining: the first pole is put next to the second
indicatorNotes.cycling: the last letter goes round to the front

blocks.note: another pole is a PALE, a wooden stake, cycled to EPAL

annotation.surface: A Polish cyclist teaming up with another rider on a tour abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland. A pale is a pointed stake, as in a paling fence.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Himalayan state between India and China.

entries.clue: Inexperienced person covering for archdeacon from island (5)

indicatorNotes.covering for: the covering of a word is its outside letters

blocks.note: a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter

annotation.surface: A novice cleric standing in for the archdeacon on an island parish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering for' reads as deputising; it means the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective of origin: the definition is vague on purpose, and any Caribbean island native would fit until the wordplay narrows it.

entries.clue: Temperature lowered in public pool for Thai rhino (5)

annotation.definitionNote: plural: rhino is uncountable slang for money

indicatorNotes.lowered: in a down answer, the T moves one place down

blocks.note: public baths are a swimming pool
T = temperature, the letter within BATHS that moves

annotation.surface: Cooling a public pool for a rhinoceros from Thailand.
annotation.walkthrough: Rhino is old British slang for money, so Thai rhino is Thai currency. BATHS becomes BAHTS by moving T down one place.
annotation.definitionFit: The baht is the currency of Thailand, and rhino is slang for money.

entries.clue: Twisted bone by sewer blocked by British fool (9)

indicatorNotes.Twisted: turned around, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.blocked by: the sewer has the British letter stuck inside it

annotation.surface: A crooked bone found in a drain that a British idiot has clogged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' here reverses rather than rearranges; with three letters the difference barely shows.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: someone supposedly with a brain as small as a bird's.

entries.clue: Tense in verse one periodically raised by Yankee (5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods, so a letter is taken at every second step through the words
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down answer, lifted to run bottom to top
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so the Yankee letter stands next to the rest

blocks.note: Y = Yankee in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An American poet anxious about his first verse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' is the adjective, anxious, not the grammar term that 'verse' nudges towards.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense: nervy means jittery, whereas in American English it more often means cheeky.

entries.clue: Take over in the air when flying without introduction of adult (7)

indicatorNotes.when flying: things sent flying scatter everywhere, so the letters land in a new order
indicatorNotes.without: the adult letter is left out
indicatorNotes.introduction of: a word is introduced by its opening letter, so only the A of adult

blocks.note: the first letter of Adult, removed

annotation.surface: A pilot taking the controls mid-flight when the grown-up is missing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a cockpit handover; take over here means receive from someone who has died.
annotation.definitionFit: To inherit is to take over property or a role from a predecessor.

entries.clue: Nick emptied tanker by one river after another (7)

indicatorNotes.emptied: the insides are removed, leaving the ends
indicatorNotes.after: the second river follows the first

blocks.note: the Ouse is one of several English rivers

annotation.surface: An empty oil tanker stolen as it moved from one river to the next.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for steal, and so is trouser, to pocket money.
annotation.definitionFit: To trouser is to pocket money, often dishonestly, so to nick it.

entries.clue: Primate keeping close to bars vaulted enclosure (4)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the primate holds the letter inside
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A zoo ape right up against the bars of its cage.
annotation.walkthrough: The zoo scene makes 'enclosure' a cage; it is the curved end of a church.
annotation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted, semicircular recess at the end of a church.

entries.clue: Good lines within contest important for future princess (5,5)

indicatorNotes.within: the lines go inside the word for important

annotation.surface: A royal-to-be learning her lines for an important part.
annotation.walkthrough: Grace Kelly was a Hollywood actress who married Prince Rainier of Monaco in 1956, hence future princess.
annotation.definitionFit: Grace Kelly became Princess Grace of Monaco, so as an actress she was a future princess.
